result.question: State-of-the-art neural-network architectures for electromagnetic calorimeter single-photon energy regression (LHCb PicoCal / CMS ECAL / similar shashlik/spaghetti calorimeters), 2022–2026, that achieve the best energy resolution and beat gradient-boosted decision trees (BDT/XGBoost). Focus on: (1) inductive biases for the additive/extensive nature of shower energy — Energy Flow Networks / Deep Sets with energy-weighted SUM pooling vs mean pooling; (2) Particle Transformer (ParT) style attention with pairwise interaction bias for calorimeter cells; (3) GravNet / Object Condensation graph networks; (4) hybrid designs that feed cluster-level aggregate features (total energy, seed energy) alongside per-cell tokens; (5) residual / learned-calibration targets (predict correction to calibrated energy sum); (6) practical resolution numbers reported and which architecture wins on clean single-particle showers. Deliver concrete, cited recommendations for the architecture and pooling/target choices most likely to beat a BDT on single-photon energy resolution.
result.summary: For clean single-photon energy regression the evidence points to a Deep Sets / Energy-Flow-Network backbone whose core inductive bias is an energy-weighted SUM over per-cell embeddings (F(Σ zᵢ Φ(xᵢ))), not mean pooling — this additive aggregation matches the extensive nature of shower energy and is infrared/collinear-safe by construction (EFN, arXiv:1810.05165; calorimeter Deep Sets, arXiv:2310.04442). The strongest published NN wins over BDT-corrected classical algorithms are modest but real: CMS DeepCluster (CNN+GNN) improves single-photon σ_E by ~10% (0.55 vs 0.61 GeV) over PFClustering+BDT (arXiv:2311.17914), and Belle II's GravNet fuzzy-clustering GNN improves low-energy photon resolution by >30% under heavy background (arXiv:2306.04179) — but crucially, in the clean zero-pileup single-EM-shower regime a GravNet+object-condensation net only TIES the calibrated baseline near the detector's intrinsic limit rather than beating it (arXiv:2204.01681). The most transferable architectural mechanisms are (a) Particle-Transformer-style attention that adds a learned pairwise-interaction matrix U as an additive pre-softmax bias, P-MHA=SoftMax(QKᵀ/√d+U)V, which beats both Deep-Sets/PFN and GravNet-style ParticleNet on jet classification (arXiv:2202.03772), and (b) hybrid designs like CMS DeepSC that feed per-cell rechit tokens alongside cluster/region aggregate features and regress a multiplicative energy CORRECTION FACTOR (residual/learned-calibration target) rather than absolute energy (arXiv:2204.10277). Concrete recommendation to beat a BDT: use per-cell tokens with an energy-weighted SUM-pooled Deep-Sets/EFN core (optionally add ParT pairwise-bias attention), concatenate cluster-level aggregates (total energy, seed energy) as extra features, and predict a residual correction to the calibrated cell-energy sum (E_rec = Σ wᵢ Eᵢ or ψ·E_dep) rather than absolute energy from scratch.

findings.claim: The additive/extensive nature of shower energy is best captured by a Deep Sets / Energy-Flow-Network core: a per-cell/per-particle latent embedding Φ followed by an energy-weighted SUM pooling (F(Σ zᵢ Φ(xᵢ))), not mean pooling. The energy-weighted sum is what makes the aggregate additive and infrared/collinear-safe BY CONSTRUCTION; uniform mean pooling is not IRC-safe. A calorimeter Deep Sets net realizes this with a plain summation over per-cell embeddings (u'=f_global(Σ vᵢ')), energy entering as a per-cell input feature, with a 4×64 per-cell MLP.
findings.evidence: EFN abstract (arXiv:1810.05165): 'These networks feature a per-particle internal (latent) representation, and summing over all particles yields an overall event-level latent representation' and 'respect infrared and collinear safety by construction.' EFN form O=F(Σᵢ zᵢ Φ(x̂ᵢ)): soft cells (zᵢ→0) contribute nothing (IR safety), collinear splits preserve the weighted sum (C safety). Calorimeter Deep Sets paper (arXiv:2310.04442) uses plain SUM aggregation u'=f_global(Σ vᵢ') with a 4-layer, 64-node per-cell MLP. Merges claims 0,1,2,3,4.

findings.claim: Particle-Transformer (ParT) style attention with a pairwise-interaction bias is directly transferable to calorimeter cells and is the strongest attention mechanism: the pairwise features are injected as a learned additive bias to the pre-softmax attention scores — P-MHA(Q,K,V)=SoftMax(QKᵀ/√d_k + U)V — where U is a learned MLP embedding of physics-designed pairwise features, NOT extra tokens or positional encodings. On the JetClass benchmark ParT beats GravNet-style ParticleNet and Deep-Sets/EFN-style PFN (accuracy 0.861 vs 0.844 vs 0.772; AUC 0.9877 vs 0.9849 vs 0.9714), with up to ~3× higher background rejection than ParticleNet.
findings.evidence: ParT paper: 'we add the interaction matrix U to the pre-softmax attention weights ... P-MHA(Q,K,V)=SoftMax(QKᵀ/√d_k+U)V ... increasing the expressiveness of the attention mechanism.' JetClass table: PFN 0.772/0.9714, ParticleNet 0.844/0.9849, ParT 0.861/0.9877. CAVEAT: these are jet-tagging CLASSIFICATION metrics, not photon energy-regression resolution — evidence is by architectural analogy, not a direct regression benchmark. Merges claims 7,8,11,12.
findings.vote: 3-0 (claims 7,8,11 unanimous; claim 12 split 2-1, dissent only on 'mean-pooled' gloss of PFN)

findings.claim: CMS DeepSC (DeepSuperCluster) is the canonical hybrid design for the RQ's items (4) and (5): it feeds per-cell rechit tokens (iη,iφ,iz,En) TOGETHER WITH cluster-level aggregates (energy, position, crystal count, seed-relative deltas) and detector-region max/min/avg summaries. A GNN layer first summarizes each cluster's rechits into a fixed-size vector before a self-attention + GCN graph over clusters (adjacency built dynamically from a learned per-cluster 3D-coordinate embedding, GravNet-style). It is multi-task and regresses an energy CORRECTION FACTOR that restores generator-level energy — a residual/learned-calibration target, not absolute energy from scratch — improving resolution ~10% over the standard CMS algorithm.
findings.evidence: arXiv:2204.10277: inputs include '(i) Energy, position and number of crystals of each cluster; (ii) ... Δη,Δφ,ΔET,ΔEn(cl,seed); (iii) List of N rechit information [(iη,iφ,iz,En)...]; (iv) Summary information for each region ... maximum, minimum, and average.' 'A GNN layer is applied on the rechits of each cluster to obtain a single fixed-size vector.' 'The adjacency matrix Aij ... assigning to each cluster a 3D-space coordinates vector with a SA layer and computing the Euclidean distance ... learned automatically.' Tasks: '(ii) Energy regression: extract the correction factor needed to restore the generator-level particle energy.' Merges claims 5,6,13,14.

findings.claim: Residual / learned-calibration targets are the recommended output parameterization: rather than regressing absolute energy, predict per-cell weights or a multiplicative correction applied to already-calibrated cell energies. Belle II's GNN predicts per-crystal weights giving E_rec = Σ wᵢ E_crystal_i (energy-weighted sum = additive/extensive bias + calibration target). HGCAL object-condensation GNNs predict a per-hit correction factor ψ≈1 applied to deposited energy, trained on the residual (E_true − ψ·E_dep). CMS DeepSC regresses a correction factor to the supercluster sum.
findings.evidence: Belle II (arXiv:2306.04179): 'E_rec^GNN = Σ wᵢ E_rec^crystal_i' — network predicts per-cell weights on calibrated crystal energies. HGCAL (EPJC 10.1140/epjc/s10052-022-10665-7 / arXiv:2204.01681): loss L_E = log(((E_true,t − ψ_h E_dep,t)/√E_true,t + 0.003)² + 1) with ψ_h≈1 a per-hit correction factor applied multiplicatively to deposited energy. Merges claims 10,19.

findings.claim: Published NN wins over BDT-corrected baselines on single-photon energy resolution are real but modest, and are largest in HARD regimes (low energy, high background, overlapping showers) rather than clean single showers. CMS DeepCluster (two-stage CNN seed-finder + GNN center-finder with message passing) beats PFClustering+BDT by ~10% (σ_E 0.55 vs 0.61 GeV, 1–100 GeV single photons). Belle II GravNet fuzzy-clustering GNN improves low-energy (E<0.5 GeV) high-background photon resolution by >30% over the classical baseline.
findings.evidence: DeepCluster (arXiv:2311.17914) Table 4: σ_E=0.55±0.00 GeV (DeepCluster) vs 0.61±0.00 GeV (PFClustering+BDT), 'the energy resolution is improved by about 10%.' PFClustering's own energy correction 'is carried out using a multivariate technique known as the Boosted Decision Trees (BDT).' Belle II abstract: '>30% for photons with energies E<0.5 GeV and high levels of beam backgrounds.' CAVEAT: DeepCluster numbers are Geant4/toy simulation, not real-data validated. Merges claims 15,16,22,23,17.
findings.vote: 3-0 (claims 15,17,22,23 unanimous; claim 16 split 2-1, dissent only on 'end-to-end' phrasing)

findings.claim: GravNet + object-condensation graph networks are a validated calorimeter architecture family (four GravNet blocks → concatenate → dense heads) that does clustering, classification, and energy/position regression end-to-end in one step. BUT the honest caveat for the RQ: in the CLEAN zero-pileup single-EM-shower regime, GravNet+object-condensation only MATCHES the calibrated baseline near the detector's intrinsic resolution limit — it does not beat it. Its advantage appears under occupancy/pileup/overlap. GravNet's neighbor aggregation is NOT confirmed to be sum-based (that specific claim was refuted).
findings.evidence: arXiv:2106.01832: 'an end-to-end machine-learning method that performs clustering, classification, and energy and position regression in one step ... We employ GravNet ... and an object condensation loss.' EPJC 2022 (arXiv:2204.01681) §8.1: 'The reconstructed energy resolution in 0 pileup for electromagnetic showers is almost indistinguishable from the baseline and, therefore, close to the detector limitations.' The stronger claim that GravNet aggregates neighbors by distance-weighted SUMMATION was REFUTED (vote 0-3) against arXiv:2306.04179. Merges claims 9,18,20,21; incorporates the one refuted claim as a caveat.
findings.vote: mixed: claim 9 split 2-1; claims 18,20,21 unanimous 3-0; associated sum-pooling claim refuted 0-3

result.caveats: Time-sensitivity / scope: all quantitative resolution numbers come from Monte-Carlo / Geant4 or toy detector simulation, not real-data validation, so the ~10% DeepCluster and >30% Belle II gains are simulation figures. Domain mismatch: none of the confirmed head-to-head resolution wins are on an LHCb PicoCal shashlik geometry specifically — the primary sources are CMS ECAL (crystals), Belle II ECL (CsI(Tl) crystals), and HGCAL (silicon/scintillator imaging). Transfer to shashlik/spaghetti sampling calorimeters is by architectural analogy, not direct benchmark. The ParT superiority evidence (0.861 vs 0.844 vs 0.772) is jet-tagging CLASSIFICATION, not energy regression — it motivates the pairwise-bias attention mechanism but is not proof it wins on single-photon σ_E. Critically for the RQ's central question ('which architecture wins on clean single showers'): the one direct clean-regime test (GravNet+object condensation at 0 pileup) shows the NN only TIES the calibrated baseline, and none of the confirmed sources demonstrate a large NN-over-BDT resolution win on genuinely clean, isolated single photons — the big gains all come from hard regimes (low energy, pileup, overlap, beam background). Two claims were split 2-1 (ParT ranking gloss; DeepCluster 'end-to-end' phrasing) but the dissents were on wording, not substance. One claim (GravNet = distance-weighted SUM pooling) was fully refuted, so do not assume GravNet's aggregation provides the additive/extensive inductive bias — that property is established for EFN/Deep-Sets energy-weighted sum pooling, not for GravNet.
openQuestions: Is there any published direct head-to-head of a neural regressor vs XGBoost/BDT on a shashlik/spaghetti (LHCb PicoCal-style) single-photon energy target, rather than crystal calorimeters — and does the NN actually beat the BDT there in the clean regime?

Does adding ParT-style pairwise-interaction-bias attention on top of an energy-weighted-sum Deep Sets core measurably improve single-photon energy RESOLUTION (not classification), and is the extra compute justified over a plain EFN for the low cell-multiplicity of a single isolated shower?

For the residual/correction-factor target, what is the best baseline to correct: raw calibrated cell-energy sum vs seed+cluster BDT output — and how much of the gain is from the additive-sum inductive bias versus from the correction-target parameterization itself (an ablation none of the sources isolate)?

Since clean single-shower gains appear small (GravNet ties baseline at 0 pileup), is the practical justification for a NN over a BDT on PicoCal primarily forward-looking robustness to pileup/minimum-bias overlap rather than clean-shower resolution — and can that be quantified for PicoCal occupancy?

refuted.claim: GravNet aggregates neighbor features by distance-weighted SUMMATION (Gaussian potential in learned latent space), confirming sum-based pooling as the aggregation inductive bias in a winning calorimeter architecture.
